state:
The bounded catalog and language-server parser is the only implementation under consideration. Inspection establishes that its tree retains source-ordered object pairs and decoded duplicate names, with first-occurrence lookup. Numeric nodes retain every legal source lexeme, even enormous magnitudes, -0 and unusual legal exponents. The existing i64 view rejects decimal/exponent syntax, whereas server request IDs use exact decimal arithmetic to admit mathematical signed-32-bit integers while retaining text for replies. A complete single JSON input and strict Rust strings/keys are required, so invalid surrogate escapes reject. A value begins at depth zero; entry above depth 64 fails during parsing. An empty array/object at depth 64 still succeeds. Caller byte decoding remains strict. Transport already limits allocation to an inclusive 64 MiB frame body. Existing reserved-envelope duplicate rejection and unknown/nested-member behavior are separate caller policies, not changes for this engine pass.
The existing dependency set already provides Serde 1.0.229 (std/derive) and serde_json 1.0.151 (std/raw_value), both without defaults. A working option A delegates grammar to the library through a bounded DeserializeSeed visitor and a reader carrying a byte cursor. The seed distinguishes root, map-value and array-value positions; numeric tokens alone pass through IgnoredAny and then retain their original source bytes. Strict string decoding and ordered visitor accumulation handle the other tokens. Around 90 lines replace around 280 legacy parser/UTF-8 lines. This works with inspected pinned internals: one-character IoRead lookahead, array token peeking before the seed and map colon consumption without peeking its value. It adds no feature or number-marker protocol, and does not ignore a whole subtree. Prototype evidence includes 297 explicit number/position expectations, 25 rejected grammar/Unicode inputs, 3 genuine marker/decoded-duplicate objects and 28 baseline depth edges. Only 66 bytes of a 20,001-byte, depth-10,000 document were read before refusal. Thirty parses of a representative mixed 360 KB document measured roughly 98 ms against 50 ms for the original engine. This suggests about twice the parser time; real compiler/server latency has yet to be tested.
Option B separates bounded strict validation from raw-value reconstruction, potentially adding arbitrary_precision and repeated traversal. That alternative is not established by tests yet. Simply using Value would discard required properties, synthetic arbitrary-precision markers need careful distinction from authored objects, and whole RawValue acceptance would miss the required Unicode/depth checks. Option C keeps the already bounded manual engine, with its demonstrated compatibility and speed and no private-reader dependency, but does not finish the requested parser removal. There is no newly demonstrated grammar bug that independently forces its removal.
ParseError currently exposes a static reason string and byte offset. Only its Display is used in production: the catalog wraps it in E6003 with the original source anchor; LSP replaces the detail with fixed invalid JSON, code -32700 and null ID. Search found no production field users or other struct constructors and no fixtures obligating the former exact reasons or positions. Although the JSON module is public, this compiler crate is unpublished and outside Rust source users were not qualified. Public Serde error categories and byte-oriented line/column locations can support conversion; specific native reasons are owned strings. We need a declared error compatibility choice, never leaked strings or a second grammar implementation to recover old prose.

engine_policy.instructions: Select the implementation path with the strongest overall fit to the required representation, admission and measured costs; do not treat untested alternatives as proven.

criteria.pinned_cursor: Release the bounded one-pass candidate after real caller checks, keeping its source-origin assumptions version-qualified and its parser-time regression visible.
criteria.two_pass: Prefer two library passes with explicit raw rebuilding, accepting additional qualification and implementation work rather than relying on reader lookahead for slices.
criteria.retain_bounded: Continue using the established bounded parser for now, documenting that the replacement objective remains open because cost and private coupling do not justify it yet.

error_policy.instructions: Given the actual field and display consumers, select a reason representation and state any deliberate compatibility differences.

criteria.static_categories: Keep the static public message and map stable error classifications to general reasons, preserving location/depth information while intentionally reducing specificity.
criteria.owned_native_reason: Change the public message to String and retain the useful library reason, with unchanged outer diagnostics and explicit disclosure of source-type, text and location drift.
criteria.mapped_static_details: Translate detailed library display prefixes into static reason constants, falling back safely; retain source type but take on a version-sensitive diagnostic table.
